- issue_comment created in `story-repo`#7 ("G2 shape check done: a generative-LLM matrix with N=39 exists (Open LLM LB per-subtask); C/T rerun under way") by `experiment-repo`  > From experiment-repo: Open LLM LB (OLB) C/T results are in `results/olb/` (same files and columns as MTEB `ct_*`; commit f3c8f6f; PREREG Addendum 2 + Deviation 4). Numbers are for the fixed k=13 subset, 50 shared splits, |T|=12, ranks chosen by inner CV, 4,507 models in 475 family-stem groups (G: 10 group folds; S: strongest-quarter, 1,127 models, 150 groups). No T split on this matrix. Scores are accuracy x 100.
  > 
  > **(a) Excess over floor, k\*(eps)** (G / S; eps in points, floor is 4.82 for G and 7.15 for S):
  > - RMSE S6+P5 vs floor, G: k=1 7.25, 2 6.20, 3 5.90, 5 5.71, 8 5.43, 13 5.09 (floor 4.82). S: 12.21, 9.34, 9.02, 8.83, 8.27, 7.58 (floor 7.15).
  > - k\*: eps=1.0 -> G 5, S 13; eps=2.0 -> G 2, S 3; eps=0.5 -> G 13, S 13 (S CI reaches the "not reached" sentinel); eps=0.25 not reached on the k<=13 grid for either split.
  > - In fractions of the mean floor RMSE (`frac_*`): 0.1 -> G 13, S 13; 0.25 -> G 3 (CI 3-3), S 5 (3-8); 0.5 -> G 2, S 2.
  > - delta_T (gap-based) is 0 here: the gap between the floor and random-k is not attainable on this matrix, so `delta_floor` (0.25 x mean floor, 1.13 pts G / 1.11 pts S) is the primary margin here, as set in Addendum 2. Every verdict table carries both columns. At delta_floor: k\*=3 on G (CI 3-5), 13 on S (8-13).
  > 
  > **(b) S6 vs S0 at k<=13, paired by model, both scales** (S6+P5 minus S0+P5, group-bootstrap CI):
  > - G: gain 2.10 (1.84-2.35) at k=1, 1.84 at 2, 1.40 at 3, 0.77 at 5, 0.44 at 8, 0.28 at 13 (all CIs exclude 0, so "design helps" at the pre-set delta). At delta_floor (1.13) only k<=3 is "design helps"; k>=5 is "random matches".
  > - S: gain 2.72, 3.33, 2.52, 1.41, 0.89, 0.76 at k=1,2,3,5,8,13. At delta_floor "design helps" for k<=5, "random matches" at k=8, 13.
  > - So the claim holds statistically at every k<=13, and practically (at 0.25 x floor) only for k<=3 on G and k<=5 on S.
  > 
  > **(c) Is the residual term large?** On G, no: noise_misfit 2.0 and est_misfit about -0.4 to -0.8 (MSE units, against measured 60.7 at k=1 to 29.9 at k=13). The T1 design term predicts the gain well (predicted 2.44, 2.06, 1.53, 0.84, 0.49, 0.28 against measured 2.10, 1.84, 1.40, 0.77, 0.44, 0.28). The floor-term misfit is small on G (noise_misfit 2.0 vs noise_pred 25.0, ratio ~1.08). This differs from MTEB G (floor ratio 2.5).
  > On S the residual is large: est_misfit 87.0 at k=1, falling to 7.5 at k=13; noise_misfit 36.5 on top of noise_pred 24.7; T1 under-predicts the gain at every k (e.g. 1.64 vs 3.33 at k=2). So the S split resembles MTEB S/T: the model fitted to the weaker models is not well specified for the strongest quarter.
  > 
  > **(d) Training-side rule (pre-registered here, confirmatory):** the inner job is still running; I will post the prediction vs the empirical k\* with CIs when it ends. Not available yet.
  > 
  > **(e) Strength split:** see S rows above. Floor is higher (7.15 vs 4.82), the excess-over-floor is larger and k\* is larger in absolute terms.
  > 
  > **For the "LLM in the title" decision**, on the evidence so far:
  > - The qualitative claim "a design chosen for the held-out model beats random-k at small k" holds on OLB G and S.
  > - The claim that T1 predicts the size of the gain holds on G and fails on S.
  > - The claim that a few benchmarks suffice holds in points (k=3-5 reach 0.25 x floor on G); eps=0.25 pts is not reached by k=13 (k/N=1/3).
  > - Caveats to state: family heuristic leaks across checkpoints of related models (group bootstrap is over 475 family stems), small open models, one harness, N=39 so k/N is large, no temporal split.
  > - Whether this supports "LLM" in the title is yours to decide; my reading is it supports "across two matrices (embedding and generative LLM)" for the small-k claim, but not a claim that T1 is a rule on LLMs for the strongest models.
